text:
Miriam: Thanks everyone for joining the infra update Q&A. Quick follow-up from the roadmap slide — folks asked for a clearer plan on regional provisioning and how the autoscaler will behave during launch windows. I'll post answers here and hand to Eng for details.
Nikhil: TL;DR: APAC pilot in late May, broader rollout in June. We're prioritizing stable capacity rather than max raw GPU count.
Tara: Re: provisioning — we've reserved two dedicated pools in SIN and one burst pool in KUL for the pilot. These are a mix of reserved and spot-backed VMs.
Sam: Can you clarify "burst pool"? Will it preempt existing Dedicated customers or only apply to Hosted?
Tara: Burst pool is strictly for Hosted API traffic with soft isolation. It won't evict Dedicated reservations. It can be reclaimed by the cloud provider (spot), so the autoscaler has fallback rules to route to nearby regions or lower-tier model variants.
Elena: What's the fallback ordering? eg. SIN -> JP -> US? Any cost impact expected?
Nikhil: Fallback policy: 1) local burst (if available), 2) dedicated local pool (if customer has reservation), 3) sister APAC region (Tokyo), 4) nearest multi-tenant in US-west as last resort. Cost-wise, cross-region egress will be accounted and billed transparently; we'll show estimates in Console before enabling cross-region fallback.
Sam: For customers with strict data residency, how do we ensure we don't route out of region?
Tara: We have an opt-in flag on the route config: "avoid-cross-region-fallback": true. When set, autoscaler will never reroute out of the pinned region and will instead queue or reject with a clear 429 + reason. We'll add this to the policy doc.
Miriam: Good — add sample config and the exact error code text in the follow-up doc.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline started for autoscaler v1.2. ETA 13:40 UTC.
Elena: Autoscaler behavior question: how do we handle sudden spikes from small customers? e.g., a PLG signup causing a burst — will we scale per-customer or global?
Nikhil: The autoscaler has two control planes: global scaling for infra (adds nodes/pools) and per-customer token-rate shaping (soft-limits). For PLG spikes we'll throttle at token-level and recommend using reserved pools for heavy sustained usage.
Sam: Any changes to the billing model for burst usage? Customers worried about surprise charges.
Tara: We'll surface a "burst allowance" window in the Console with an estimated cost delta. Default is conservative; customers can opt into higher burst windows and see projected spend. We'll also send usage alerts when burst spend exceeds threshold X% of monthly commit.
Elena: Ops question: what's the SLO for cold-start latency when spinning a new node in APAC?
Nikhil: Target cold-start <= 90s for node provisioning, warm-up + model load median ~ 25s for smaller 7B variants, up to 75s for 70B. We mitigate by pre-warming commonly used model variants based on traffic forecasts.
Sam: Is there an immediate action item for platform teams?
Tara: Yes — (1) add the "avoid-cross-region-fallback" flag to route schema PR by EOD Friday, (2) Console team to show burst allowance opt-in in the Billing page by next sprint, (3) SRE to validate cold-start telemetry for APAC pilot.
Miriam: I'll follow up with customers on dedicated reservation offsets for APAC. Thanks.
Elena: One last ask — can we add a simple FAQ: "What happens if my model is evicted from spot?" Many customers asked.
Nikhil: Will add: short answer — we transparently failover to reserved or sister-region variant with a one-line public explanation and a trace ID for debugging.
Sam: :thumbsup: Thanks team.
Tara: I'll open the PRs and tag @eng-sre and @console.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline finished successfully for autoscaler v1.2.
Miriam: Great, closing this thread — I'll paste follow-up doc and actions in #product-update later today.
